slice: G4b: M-15 (spawn exemption must key on animation AND direction row), M-33 (interact latch on a recycled proxy), M-43 (camera sway constructor), plus the deferred P3 comment of AlundraPlayerManager.cs:309-310 (critic-corrected report)
summary:
Read-only critique. I re-disassembled and re-read the decision-carrying points; nothing was built, run or written to the repository. The core of the discovery report holds, with six corrections and four upgrades.

M-15 (CONFIRMED): the binary has no exemption flag; its switch test in UpdateAnimation (0x80038AB4) is on the pair (Target != Current at 0x80038B08) OR (row from table[AnimationDirection*8+col(TargetDirection)] != AnimationDirection at 0x80038B10). InitializeEntity (0x80039D04) writes Current=~anim, CurrentDirection=~dir, Target, TargetDirection, then calls UpdateAnimation (0x80039EA8), which commits (anim, row R0) and writes +0xF8; the next UpdateAnimation clears +0xF8 first (0x80038AE4). So the binary's effective exemption keys on animation AND row: any later change of either before the first validation is an ordinary switch with an impulse. The DLL compares the animation only (AlundraFrameSyncPasses.cs:128, :266) and, deeper, does not commit the spawn row at spawn (AnimationDirection is assigned only at AlundraFrameSyncPasses.cs:140), so a pre-validation turn resolves from row 0 instead of R0. The table in the EXE (0x800237F4) is identical to AnimationTables.cs:30-36. Exposure today: no real site found by census and reading (not a measurement).

M-33 (CONFIRMED as a real latent port defect, not original behaviour): the binary latch holds a slot pointer (0x80098F0C) plus the serial Index2 (+4, stored in 0x80126F64) and compares the serial first (0x8002E9B4-0x8002E9C0); a freed slot is overwritten by the zero BSS template (so Index2 = 0, while live serials start at 1), and a reused slot gets a new serial, so the latch can never survive a recycle. In the DLL Index2 is never assigned and the recycler keeps Flags, ProgramIndexes and Pos, so a latched recycled proxy is still found. The test-hygiene half was closed by E19.m5 (e35cd5e). Corrections to the report: the guard must reject BOTH Destroyed and FlagToDestroy for a binary-faithful result (the report's own optional control test was wrong, it is a RED test), the 'eager clear' alternative is not equivalent, and a guard on the latch term alone leaves the adjacent stale-XCollisionEntity branch (not shown reachable).

M-43: accept with the written reason (deliberate internal constructor, comment at AlundraCameraSway.cs:25, 15 test constructions in 2 files).

P3 comment: stale on both counts (LoadingMap ported by E19.v, air states by E19.d2c2). The report's replacement wording would have duplicated the existing 'USER DECISION' sentence; corrected wording is in production_change. The class doc has further stale statements outside the slice.

facts.claim: The binary's switch test is on the pair (animation, direction row); +0xF8 is cleared on every call before the test; the new row is stored at +0x98 and +0xF8 receives the animation set's IsZForceApplied only inside the switch block. RE-VERIFIED.
facts.evidence: python docs/plan-e19-backlog-1006-annexe/mipsdis.py 80038AB4 60: 0x80038AD8 lw a2,0x88 (Target); 0x80038ADC lw a3,0x98 (AnimationDirection); 0x80038AE0 lw v0,0x8c (TargetDirection); 0x80038AE4 sw zero,0xf8; 0x80038AE8-0x80038AFC row address = 0x800237F4 + AD*32 + ((TD+2)&0x1c), a1 = table value; 0x80038B00 lw v0,0x90 (Current); 0x80038B08 bne a2,v0 -> switch; 0x80038B10 beq a1,a3 -> skip (no switch); 0x80038B40 sw a1,0x98; 0x80038B4C sw a2,0x90; 0x80038B5C-0x80038B64 lh 0xA(animSet) -> +0xF8.

facts.claim: AD_init is 0 in the binary, now MEASURED instead of inferred from Entity.Clear(): the slot template at 0x80134368 lies beyond the end of the file-backed image (0x800CA800), so it is BSS (zero at boot); the only store into it found is 0x8003B21C (+0x48 = -1); the other references to the template base (0x8003864C, 0x8003A074, 0x8003A0E8, 0x8003B264) are copy loops that read FROM it. facts.claim: The binary latch: slot pointer at 0x80098F0C, serial at 0x80126F64, entity position at 0x80126F58/5C/60, player position at 0x80126F48/4C/50, direction at 0x80126F54. On the latch path the serial (+4) is compared first, then the three entity positions, the three player positions, then TargetDirection; any mismatch goes to 0x8002EA78 which zeroes the pointer and leaves collided = XCollisionEntity. The final check reads ProgramIndexes[5] (+0x60) / SpriteProgramIndexes[5] (+0x84), Flags & 0x8000 (+0x6C) and the Square bit 0x80 of the just-pressed word. RE-VERIFIED against the decompilation (PlayerManager.cs:1597-1669, matches the DLL branch for branch).

production_change:
M-33 (about 4 lines, plus the optional adjacent branch). In AlundraPlayerManager.CheckEntityInteraction add a private static predicate IsRecycledSlot(AlundraEntityScriptProxy p) => p.Status is EntityStatus.Destroyed or EntityStatus.FlagToDestroy and add '&& !IsRecycledSlot(state.InteractLatchEntity)' to the all-equal conjunction of the latch test (:650-657). A mismatch then takes the existing fall-through (:681-686: latch = null, collidedEntity = XCollisionEntity), which is exactly the binary's serial mismatch on a wiped slot (0x8002E9C0 -> 0x8002EA78). Reject BOTH states: the binary never shows a flagged slot at MovePlayer (UpdateDestroyedEntities runs first), while the DLL recycles after the entity pass, so only the two-state guard reproduces the binary's observable behaviour; if the flagged state turns out to be unreachable the second state costs nothing. Optional second hunk, only with its own RED test and only if the author wants the adjacent branch: when player.XCollisionEntity is itself a recycled slot, treat it as the wiped slot of the binary (no relatch, latch = null, result 0), since falling through with collidedEntity = XCollisionEntity would still read its kept ProgramIndexes. Correct the doc at AlundraGameState.cs:149-152 (Index2 is never assigned, so the eight checks do not self-invalidate a recycled proxy; the guard does). Add an '## Amendment (E19.m, G4b)' to ADR-0024 saying the binary overwrites the whole 0x294-byte slot (state, serial, flags, programs, positions) while the DLL keeps a deliberate partial reset and guards the one reader that can still reach a recycled proxy. Alternatives considered: (a) mint Index2 from a counter at both spawn paths and zero it in the recycler (the faithful mechanism, larger, many montages build proxies with Index2 0, better done with E14 together with the other pointer-plus-serial checks); (b) eager clear of InteractLatchEntity inside RecycleDestroyedEntities: NOT equivalent to the guard (correction to the report), it covers the recycled state only and leaves the flagged window open, and it adds a second writer of a field documented as single-writer.
